basemessage.description: Reference to a base definition for this definition. Relative references are XIDs within the same registry. Absolute URIs reference message definitions in external registries. The base definition is overridden by this definition. If not present, this definition does not override any base definition

envelope.description: Message envelope format identifier. This attribute MUST be the same as the 'envelope' attribute of the definition group, but is not automatically inherited because definitions may be cross-referenced across groups. The predefined envelope format is 'CloudEvents/1.0'

protocol.description: Protocol identifier. This attribute MUST be the same as the 'protocol' attribute of the definition group, but is not automatically inherited because definitions may be cross-referenced across groups

dataschemaformat.description: The schema format applicable to the message payload, equivalent to the 'format' attribute of the schema registry

dataschema.description: The inline schema for the message payload, equivalent to the 'schema' attribute of the schema registry

dataschemauri.description: The URI of the schema for the message payload, equivalent to the 'schemauri' attribute of the schema registry

dataschemaxid.description: Contains the xid of the xRegistry schema Resource entity associated with the dataschemauri referenced schema document. Note that this means the entity MUST be located within the same Registry.

datacontenttype.description: The content type for the message payload

envelopemetadata.description: CloudEvents attribute declarations, adding constraints to the CloudEvents envelope not yet covered by the CloudEvents spec https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md This declaration object is opaque to the Core attribute walker so literal null value constraints and protocol-defined property names are preserved. Message domain property-definition validation and defaults remain mandatory.

mode.description: Whether CloudEvents 'binary' or 'structured' mode will be used

format.description: The media type format used to serialize the CloudEvent in the case of mode=structured

properties.description: AMQP properties section https://docs.oasis-open.org/amqp/core/v1.0/os/amqp-core-messaging-v1.0-os.html#type-properties This declaration object is opaque to the Core attribute walker so literal null value constraints and protocol-defined property names are preserved. Message domain property-definition validation and defaults remain mandatory.

applicationProperties.description: AMQP application-properties section https://docs.oasis-open.org/amqp/core/v1.0/os/amqp-core-messaging-v1.0-os.html#type-application-properties This declaration object is opaque to the Core attribute walker so literal null value constraints and protocol-defined property names are preserved. Message domain property-definition validation and defaults remain mandatory.

messageAnnotations.description: AMQP message-annotations section https://docs.oasis-open.org/amqp/core/v1.0/os/amqp-core-messaging-v1.0-os.html#type-message-annotations This declaration object is opaque to the Core attribute walker so literal null value constraints and protocol-defined property names are preserved. Message domain property-definition validation and defaults remain mandatory.

deliveryAnnotations.description: AMQP delivery-annotations section https://docs.oasis-open.org/amqp/core/v1.0/os/amqp-core-messaging-v1.0-os.html#type-delivery-annotations This declaration object is opaque to the Core attribute walker so literal null value constraints and protocol-defined property names are preserved. Message domain property-definition validation and defaults remain mandatory.

footer.description: AMQP footer section https://docs.oasis-open.org/amqp/core/v1.0/os/amqp-core-messaging-v1.0-os.html#type-footer This declaration object is opaque to the Core attribute walker so literal null value constraints and protocol-defined property names are preserved. Message domain property-definition validation and defaults remain mandatory.

envelope.description: Envelope format identifier that defines the common metadata information for the message. All definitions in this group share this envelope format. Mixed-envelope-format groups are not permitted. The predefined envelope format is CloudEvents/1.0

protocol.description: Protocol identifier that defines the transport message protocol. All definitions in this group share this protocol type. Mixed-protocol groups are not permitted. Predefined protocol formats are 'AMQP/1.0', 'MQTT/3.1.1', 'MQTT/5.0', 'KAFKA', 'HTTP', and 'NATS'

type.description: The authentication/authorization type. OAuth2, Plain, APIKey, X509Cert, and SASL are well-defined

mechanism.description: The SASL mechanism name when authorization.type is SASL (for example PLAIN, SCRAM-SHA-256, SCRAM-SHA-512, OAUTHBEARER, or EXTERNAL)

resourceuri.description: The resource uri for which authorization shall be granted (if applicable)

authorityuri.description: The authority uri where authorization shall be requested (if applicable)

usage.description: Required endpoint roles: subscriber, consumer, or producer. The Endpoint specification defines allowed combinations by protocol. These are domain constraints; the Core model's scalar enum aspect does not apply to arrays.

deprecated.description: Indicates whether the endpoint is deprecated

envelope.description: Envelope metadata format identifier. If set, all definitions MUST use this format value

protocol.description: Endpoint protocol identifier. If set, all definitions MUST use this protocol value

messagegroups.description: The message groups that are supported by this endpoint. Relative references are XIDs within the same registry. Absolute URIs reference message groups in external registries.

endpoints.description: The network addresses that are for communication with the endpoint. The endpoints are ordered by preference, with the first endpoint being the preferred endpoint. Some protocol implementations might not support multiple endpoints, in which case all but the first endpoint might be ignored. Whether the URI just identifies a network host or links directly to a resource managed by the network host is protocol specific

authorization.description: Authorization options. These are hints for the adapter for interacting with the authorization endpoint. This is not a credentials configuration

deployed.description: If `true`, the endpoint metadata represents a public endpoint that is expected to be available for communication

node.description: The AMQP node name. Commonly the name of a queue or a topic. Corresponds to the 'address' in source or target of the attach frame.

durable.description: Whether the AMQP node identified by 'node' is durable rather than transient. This is a property of the node, not of the link terminus and not of the message header field of the same name. Terminus durability is expressed by 'terminus-durability'

linkProperties.description: An optional map of AMQP link properties to use with the endpoint

connectionProperties.description: An optional map of AMQP connection properties to use with the endpoint

distributionMode.description: The AMQP source distribution mode. 'move' means a transferred message is removed from the node and is therefore seen by only one receiver. 'copy' means the message remains at the node after transfer and may also be transferred to other receivers. This does not describe message locking

connectionCapabilities.description: The AMQP capabilities to use with the endpoint

nodeCapabilities.description: The AMQP node capabilities to use with the endpoint

sourceFilters.description: AMQP source filters used for subscription/receive setup

dynamic.description: Whether a dynamic source or target is requested

terminusDurability.description: Durability mode for the applicable source/target terminus

expiryPolicy.description: Expiry policy for the applicable source/target terminus

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds for the applicable expiry policy

senderSettleMode.description: AMQP sender settle mode requested for the link. It constrains the party that sends transfers over the link: the client for a producer endpoint, the remote node for a consumer endpoint

receiverSettleMode.description: AMQP receiver settle mode requested for the link. It constrains the party that receives transfers over the link: the remote node for a producer endpoint, the client for a consumer endpoint
